>> About the "special lvl settings" list

these are extra level settings which are not stored inside the level codes themselves, so if you want to change the behaviour of a certain level, you might need to edit this list.

here's what the numbers mean:

0 - has scroll stop at end of lvl (scroll stop position determined by "level end pos" list)
1 - pink key coin notice
2 - race-type level
3 - has boss
4 - final level - level will end with unique animation and will show the ending screen
5 - level doesn't contain green coins

NOTE: each item in the list corresponds to each level of the game, including hub world (the first item in the list)

>> ABOUT PORTING MIKE MAKER LEVEL CODES TO MIKE WORLD 2:

As stated earlier, levels in Mike World 2 are stored in the "official" list and use the same format as Mike Maker. This means you can replace (or add) an item in the official list with a Mike Maker level code and it should load. However, there are some differences between the two games, so you may need to make some adjustments to your level to better suit Mike World 2. The differences are listed below:

-10 coins will turn into green coins (the first green coin of a stage to be precise), so make sure you replace them with the new, working version of 10 coins, which you can access in the editor.

-some moving objects (e.g. sawblades) move at different distances due to mike world 2 levels having smaller tiles/more zoomed out camera. keep this in mind and make adjustments to your levels if this is a problem for you

-if the level stops scrolling before you reach the goal, either edit the item corresponding to the level in the "special lvl settings" list and remove the "0" (zero) from the value (do NOT delete the list item though!!! and don't remove the other numbers) or change the item corresponding to the level in the "level end pos" list to a greater value (p.s. remember in both the "special lvl settings" and "level end pos lists", the first item is for the hub world, then next is level 1, 2, 3, etc)

-mike runs faster and jumps higher in this game compared to mike maker, please bare this in mind to avoid any exploits/cheese in your level that may have not been possible with mike maker physics.

-mike world 1 themes will have the wrong music or none at all. this is done to save the project size. you can extract the missing songs from the mike maker project and import them into the backdrops sprite here to make them work. check the "play music" broadcast receiver in the backdrop scripts to check the music file names

>> DEV GUIDE - INTRODUCTION

===================================================================================================================================

Anyone can learn how to make a remix of Super Mike World 2 with fully custom levels by following this useful and in-depth guide!

Super Mike World 2 is built upon the Mike Maker engine rather than the original Mike World, so porting your own original levels from Mike Maker or creating new ones here is easy, though I highly recommend reading all the notes here before doing anything since there are a few important things you need to know, especially for when porting Mike Maker levels.

If you're wondering why I've created this guide, it's because I felt that I should try to encourage remixing of my work more, as well as for you to continue Mike's adventures since I won't be making any more Mike World games here on Scratch. Looking forward to see what you come up with!

If you're having any trouble with anything, make sure to read all the notes carefully, but if you're still struggling, send me a question on my profile.

Also, please do not attempt to steal this game and pass it off as entirely your own - remember to credit me and share it as a remix, not a re-uploaded project!

Thank you, and I hope you have fun! :)

===================================================================================================================================

>> ADDING NEW FEATURES:

I won't write too much here since explaining exactly how to create new features would be very hard and would take a really long time, also a lot of it is up to you, but here's some key info:

[==Creating new objects: You'll want to modify the "solid objects" and "non-solid objects" sprites. They work pretty much in the exact same way, except they rely on different lists and stuff, contain different objects with unique sprites and scripts and of course the solid objects act as ground for the player.

Different objects have different IDs, which are used to identify each object. There are two sets of object IDs, ones for solid objects and ones for non-solid objects. Objects can also have different varients, e.g. different types of springs. These can be selected within the editor by using these 3 variables --------->

To actual create new objects using IDs, you can use the "id" and "vari" variables within each object sprite to code what new objects should do, how they should act, etc through the use of clones, you can just add to the existing scripts for costumes, main functions, etc, no need to create a completely new script unless you're doing something complex or making moving objects. The next available ID for non-solid objects is 21 and for solid objects it's 8.

[==Creating new powerups: To creating blocks containing new power-ups, simply place down a ! block, but manually set the "cursor object var" to 04 or above before placing it. (01 = fire flower, 02 = coin, 03 = boost flower) Look, here's a handy block just for that! ----------------------------------------------------------->

New powerups will have weird black box sprites since powerups with high IDs obviously don't exist yet, but you can just copy the boost flower sprite inside "non-solid objs" and the "blockeditor3" sprite in "solid objs" and replace the 3s with 4s or whatever ID you use.

As for actually making the power-ups function, you'll need to go into the "player" sprite's code. Head to the broadcast script marked by a note saying "POWER-UP ABILITIES" near the top-right of the page to add in power-up functionality, obviously how this works is entirely up to you, and go to the part of the looooong main player script marked by a note saying "POWER-UP COLOURS" to set what colour or other effect you want the player to have while using this power-up.

[==Creating new themes: Honestly you could just replace the existing sprites/music for existing themes, but if you want to add more rather than replace them then here's how:

Backdrops: Create a sprite named bgX (X being the theme ID, 14 is the next available theme ID)

Parallax background: Go to the "bg" sprite and create costumes named "X-1", "X-2" and "X-3" inside it (X being the theme ID, you get it), with X-3 being closest, X-1 being furthest away

Ground tiles: Go to "solid objects", go to costumes and create ground tile sprites (ground 1-X ... ground 6-X, yes it's the opposite order to the bg costumes). Ground 1 to 3 is for the ground surface and ground 4 to 6 is for underneath surface tiles. You'll also need to make blockX, slopeLX and slopeRX sprites too if you use these block in your levels.

Music: Head to the backdrop code and add a new "music ( song )" custom block to the "set lvl music" function, with the ID being something new for when your lvl theme is active. Then in the "play music" broadcast reciever add a new music loop for when the value for the "music" variable is what you chose earlier.

Oh, and press this while editing your level to set the custom theme ---------------------------------------->
